```{r}
# Install (if missing) and load the required packages
if (!require("dplyr")) {
  install.packages("dplyr", dependencies = TRUE)
  library("dplyr")
}

if (!require("ggplot2")) {
  install.packages("ggplot2", dependencies = TRUE)
  library("ggplot2")
}

if (!require("tidyverse")) {
  install.packages("tidyverse", dependencies = TRUE)
  library("tidyverse")
}

# Plain number format and wide console output
options(scipen = 999, width = 150)


# ==================================================================================================
# Task 1: Preliminary data analysis
# ==================================================================================================
# Load the data
data_telemetry <- read.csv("X.csv")     # inputs x1-x4
data_power     <- read.csv("y.csv")     # output y
data_time      <- read.csv("time.csv")  # sampling time (seconds)

# Combine into one data frame
server_data <- cbind(data_time, data_telemetry, data_power)

time_col <- server_data$time_seconds
power_col <- server_data$power_consumption
signal_labels <- c("x1", "x2", "x3", "x4", "y")

# Signal labels for tables and plots
signal_names <- c("CPU Utilization", "Memory Usage", "Disk I/O", "Network Traffic", "Power Consumption")
clean_labels <- paste0(signal_labels, " ( ", signal_names, " )")


# ==================================================================================================
# Helper functions and plot style
# ==================================================================================================

# Print a titled table (text left-aligned, numbers right-aligned)
show_table <- function(title, table) {
  for (j in seq_along(table)) {
    values <- as.character(table[[j]])
    if (!all(grepl("^[-0-9.,% ]+$", values))) {
      padded <- format(c(names(table)[j], values), justify = "left")
      names(table)[j] <- padded[1]
      table[[j]]      <- padded[-1]
    }
  }
  cat("\n", strrep("=", 90), "\n  ", title, "\n", strrep("=", 90), "\n", sep = "")
  print(table, row.names = FALSE, right = TRUE)
  cat("\n")
}

# Format to 6 significant digits
num <- function(x, digits = 6) {
  trimws(formatC(x, digits = digits, format = "fg", big.mark = ","))
}

# Format to fixed decimals with thousands separators
dec <- function(x, decimals = 2) {
  formatC(x, format = "f", digits = decimals, big.mark = ",")
}

# Skewness (0 = symmetric)
skewness <- function(x) mean((x - mean(x))^3) / mean((x - mean(x))^2)^1.5

# Excess kurtosis (0 = Gaussian)
excess_kurtosis <- function(x) mean((x - mean(x))^4) / mean((x - mean(x))^2)^2 - 3

# Format p-values
p_text <- function(p) ifelse(p < 0.001, "< 0.001", dec(p, 3))

# Convert R term names to model term names, e.g. "I(x1^3)" -> "x1^3", "(Intercept)" -> "bias"
term_name <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("^I\\((.*)\\)$", "\\1", x)
  x[x == "(Intercept)"] <- "bias"
  x
}

# Convert R term names to parameter names (theta1, theta2, ..., theta_bias)
theta_name <- function(x, all_names) {
  model_terms <- all_names[all_names != "(Intercept)"]
  ifelse(x == "(Intercept)", "theta_bias", paste0("theta", match(x, model_terms)))
}

# Color scheme
COLOR_INPUT       <- "#2a78d6"  # inputs x1-x4
COLOR_INPUT_DARK  <- "#184f95"  # input lines
COLOR_OUTPUT      <- "#eb6834"  # output y
COLOR_OUTPUT_DARK <- "#b4471c"  # output lines
COLOR_MODEL       <- "#1baf7a"  # model results (residuals, predictions, posterior)
COLOR_MODEL_DARK  <- "#11805a"  # model result lines
COLOR_REFERENCE   <- "#52514e"  # reference lines
COLOR_SUMMARY     <- "#0b0b0b"  # posterior mean

signal_colors <- c(rep(COLOR_INPUT, 4), COLOR_OUTPUT)
signal_dark    <- c(rep(COLOR_INPUT_DARK, 4), COLOR_OUTPUT_DARK)

# Transparent version of a color
see_through <- function(color, opacity) adjustcolor(color, alpha.f = opacity)

# Set the panel grid and axis style
start_figure <- function(rows, cols) {
  top_margin <- if (rows * cols == 1) 1 else 3
  par(mfrow = c(rows, cols), mar = c(4.5, 5, top_margin, 1), oma = c(0, 0, 2.5, 0),
      las = 1, mgp = c(3.4, 0.7, 0), tcl = -0.3,
      cex.main = 1.05, cex.lab = 0.95, cex.axis = 0.85)
}

# Add the figure title and reset the layout
finish_figure <- function(title) {
  mtext(title, outer = TRUE, line = 0.8, font = 2, cex = 1.2)
  par(mfrow = c(1, 1), oma = c(0, 0, 0, 0), mar = c(5.1, 4.1, 4.1, 2.1))
}

# Draw the color key in an empty panel
legend_panel <- function(labels, colors = NA, pch = NA, lty = NA, lwd = NA,
                         fill = NULL, cex = 0.9) {
  plot.new()
  if (is.null(fill)) {
    legend("center", legend = labels, col = colors, pch = pch, lty = lty, lwd = lwd,
           pt.cex = 1.5, bty = "n", cex = cex, title = "Color key", title.font = 2,
           y.intersp = 1.1, xpd = NA)
  } else {
    legend("center", legend = labels, fill = fill, border = NA,
           bty = "n", cex = cex, title = "Color key", title.font = 2,
           y.intersp = 1.1, xpd = NA)
  }
}

```

# Task 1.2: Distribution for each signal
# ==================================================================================================

```{r}
start_figure(3, 2)

# Histogram of each signal
for (i in 2:ncol(server_data)) {
  values      <- server_data[ ,i]
  sig_density <- density(values)
  sig_hist    <- hist(values, breaks = 30, plot = FALSE)
  normal_peak <- dnorm(mean(values), mean(values), sd(values))
  hist(values, prob = TRUE, breaks = 30,
       ylim   = c(0, max(sig_hist$density, sig_density$y, normal_peak) * 1.05),
       col    = see_through(signal_colors[i - 1], 0.6),
       border = "white",
       main   = paste("Distribution:", clean_labels[i - 1]),
       xlab   = clean_labels[i - 1],
       ylab   = "Density")
  # Density curve and normal curve (shows how close each signal is to Gaussian)
  lines(sig_density, col = signal_dark[i - 1], lwd = 2)
  curve(dnorm(x, mean(values), sd(values)), add = TRUE, col = COLOR_REFERENCE, lwd = 2, lty = 2)
}
legend_panel(c("Input signal (x1 - x4)", "Input density curve",
               "Output signal (y)", "Output density curve", "Normal curve (same mean, SD)"),
             c(see_through(COLOR_INPUT, 0.6), COLOR_INPUT_DARK,
               see_through(COLOR_OUTPUT, 0.6), COLOR_OUTPUT_DARK, COLOR_REFERENCE),
             pch = c(15, NA, 15, NA, NA), lty = c(NA, 1, NA, 1, 2), lwd = c(NA, 2, NA, 2, 2))
finish_figure("Task 1.2: Distribution of Each Signal")
```

# ==================================================================================================
# Task 1.3: Correlation and scatter plots (input metrics vs output power)
# ==================================================================================================

```{r}
vault_telemetry <- server_data[, 2:(ncol(server_data) - 1)]
vault_power     <- server_data[, ncol(server_data)]

# One simple linear model per input: power ~ x
simple_fits <- lapply(vault_telemetry, function(x) lm(vault_power ~ x))

# Correlation between each input and the output
cor_matrix <- cor(x = vault_telemetry, y = vault_power, use = "complete.obs")

# p-value (significance) and Spearman correlation (non-linear monotonic dependence)
pearson_p <- sapply(vault_telemetry, function(x) cor.test(x, vault_power)$p.value)
spearman  <- cor(vault_telemetry, vault_power, method = "spearman")

show_table("Task 1.3.1: Correlation between each Input and the Output Power",
           data.frame(Input                 = clean_labels[1:4],
                      "Correlation (r)"           = dec(cor_matrix[, 1], 4),
                      "p-value"     = p_text(pearson_p),
                      "Rank correlation"        = dec(spearman[, 1], 4),
                      Intercept         = dec(sapply(simple_fits, function(m) coef(m)[1]), 4),
                      Slope             = dec(sapply(simple_fits, function(m) coef(m)[2]), 4),
                      check.names = FALSE))
```

# ==================================================================================================
# Task 2: Regression - modelling the relationship between server metrics
# ==================================================================================================

```{r}
# ==================================================================================================
# Data Preparation
# ==================================================================================================
# Output
server_data$y <- server_data$power_consumption

# Inputs
server_data$x1 <- server_data$cpu_utilization
server_data$x2 <- server_data$memory_usage
server_data$x3 <- server_data$disk_io
server_data$x4 <- server_data$network_traffic


# ==================================================================================================
# Building the 5 Candidate Polynomial Models
# ==================================================================================================
# Model 1: y = theta1*x4 + theta2*x1^2 + theta3*x1^3 + theta4*x2^4 + theta5*x1^4 + bias
model_1 <- lm(y ~ x4 + I(x1^2) + I(x1^3) + I(x2^4) + I(x1^4), data = server_data)

# Model 2: y = theta1*x4 + theta2*x1^3 + theta3*x3^4 + bias
model_2 <- lm(y ~ x4 + I(x1^3) + I(x3^4), data = server_data)

# Model 3: y = theta1*x3^3 + theta2*x3^4 + bias
model_3 <- lm(y ~ I(x3^3) + I(x3^4), data = server_data)

# Model 4: y = theta1*x2 + theta2*x1^3 + theta3*x3^4 + bias
model_4 <- lm(y ~ x2 + I(x1^3) + I(x3^4), data = server_data)

# Model 5: y = theta1*x4 + theta2*x1^2 + theta3*x1^3 + theta4*x3^4 + bias
model_5 <- lm(y ~ x4 + I(x1^2) + I(x1^3) + I(x3^4), data = server_data)

all_models <- list(model_1, model_2, model_3, model_4, model_5)

```
# ==================================================================================================
# Task 2.1: Estimate Model Parameters (theta_hat) for Each Model
# ==================================================================================================

```{r}
# Model equations
show_table("Task 2.1: Candidate Model Equations",
           data.frame(Model = paste("Model", 1:5),
                      Equation = sapply(all_models, function(fit) {
                        terms <- term_name(names(coef(fit))[-1])
                        paste0("y = ", paste0("theta", seq_along(terms), "*", terms, collapse = " + "),
                               " + bias")
                      })))

# Parameter estimates ("-" = not in the model)
parameter_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:5, function(m) {
  est    <- coef(all_models[[m]])
  thetas <- c(num(unname(est[-1])), rep("-", 6 - length(est)))
  data.frame(Model = paste("Model", m),
             theta1 = thetas[1], theta2 = thetas[2], theta3 = thetas[3],
             theta4 = thetas[4], theta5 = thetas[5],
             theta_bias = num(unname(est[1])))
}))
show_table("Task 2.1: Least Squares Estimates of the Model Parameters", parameter_table)
```

# ==================================================================================================
# Task 2.2: Compute Sum of Squared Errors (SSE) for Each Model
# ==================================================================================================

```{r}
# Residuals
res_1 <- residuals(model_1)
res_2 <- residuals(model_2)
res_3 <- residuals(model_3)
res_4 <- residuals(model_4)
res_5 <- residuals(model_5)
residual_list <- list(res_1, res_2, res_3, res_4, res_5)

# Sum of squared errors
SSE_Model_1 <- sum(res_1^2)
SSE_Model_2 <- sum(res_2^2)
SSE_Model_3 <- sum(res_3^2)
SSE_Model_4 <- sum(res_4^2)
SSE_Model_5 <- sum(res_5^2)

# R-squared (share of the variation in y explained by each model)
SST <- sum((server_data$y - mean(server_data$y))^2)
SSE_all <- c(SSE_Model_1, SSE_Model_2, SSE_Model_3, SSE_Model_4, SSE_Model_5)

show_table("Task 2.2: Residual Sum of Squares (SSE) for Each Model",
           data.frame(Model = paste("Model", 1:5),
                      SSE = dec(SSE_all),
                      "R-squared" = dec(1 - SSE_all / SST, 4),
                      check.names = FALSE))
```

# ==================================================================================================
# Task 2.3: Compute Log-Likelihood for Each Model
# ==================================================================================================

```{r}
logLike_Model_1 <- as.numeric(logLik(model_1))
logLike_Model_2 <- as.numeric(logLik(model_2))
logLike_Model_3 <- as.numeric(logLik(model_3))
logLike_Model_4 <- as.numeric(logLik(model_4))
logLike_Model_5 <- as.numeric(logLik(model_5))

show_table("Task 2.3: Log-Likelihood for Each Model",
           data.frame(Model = paste("Model", 1:5),
                      "Log-Likelihood" = dec(c(logLike_Model_1, logLike_Model_2, logLike_Model_3,
                                               logLike_Model_4, logLike_Model_5)),
                      check.names = FALSE))

```

# ==================================================================================================
# Task 2.4: Compute AIC and BIC for Each Model
# ==================================================================================================

```{r}
# Akaike Information Criterion (AIC)
AIC_1 <- AIC(model_1)
AIC_2 <- AIC(model_2)
AIC_3 <- AIC(model_3)
AIC_4 <- AIC(model_4)
AIC_5 <- AIC(model_5)

# Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC)
BIC_1 <- BIC(model_1)
BIC_2 <- BIC(model_2)
BIC_3 <- BIC(model_3)
BIC_4 <- BIC(model_4)
BIC_5 <- BIC(model_5)

show_table("Task 2.4: AIC and BIC for Each Model",
           data.frame(Model = paste("Model", 1:5),
                      AIC = dec(c(AIC_1, AIC_2, AIC_3, AIC_4, AIC_5)),
                      BIC = dec(c(BIC_1, BIC_2, BIC_3, BIC_4, BIC_5))))
```

# ==================================================================================================
# Task 2.5: Distribution of Model Prediction Errors (Residuals) and Q-Q Plots
# ==================================================================================================

```{r}
# Residual histograms with density curve
start_figure(2, 3)

for (m in 1:5) {
  res <- residual_list[[m]]
  res_density <- density(res)
  res_hist    <- hist(res, breaks = 30, plot = FALSE)
  hist(res, prob = TRUE, breaks = 30,
       ylim   = c(0, max(res_hist$density, res_density$y, dnorm(mean(res), mean(res), sd(res))) * 1.05),
       col    = see_through(COLOR_MODEL, 0.6),
       border = "white",
       main   = paste("Residual Distribution: Model", m),
       xlab   = "Residual (prediction error)",
       ylab   = "Density")
  lines(res_density, col = COLOR_MODEL_DARK, lwd = 2)
  # Normal curve with the same mean and SD (comparison with a Gaussian shape)
  curve(dnorm(x, mean(res), sd(res)), add = TRUE, col = COLOR_REFERENCE, lwd = 2, lty = 2)
  abline(v = 0, col = COLOR_REFERENCE, lwd = 1.5, lty = 3)
}
legend_panel(c("Residuals (histogram)", "Density curve", "Normal curve (same mean, SD)", "Zero error"),
             c(see_through(COLOR_MODEL, 0.6), COLOR_MODEL_DARK, COLOR_REFERENCE, COLOR_REFERENCE),
             pch = c(15, NA, NA, NA), lty = c(NA, 1, 2, 3), lwd = c(NA, 2, 2, 1.5))
finish_figure("Task 2.5.1: Distribution of the Model Residuals")
```

```{r}
# Normal Q-Q plots
start_figure(2, 3)

for (m in 1:5) {
  qqnorm(residual_list[[m]], pch = 16, cex = 0.7,
         col  = see_through(COLOR_MODEL_DARK, 0.6),
         main = paste("Normal Q-Q: Model", m))
  qqline(residual_list[[m]], col = COLOR_REFERENCE, lwd = 2)
}
legend_panel(c("Residual quantiles", "Normal reference line"),
             c(COLOR_MODEL_DARK, COLOR_REFERENCE),
             pch = c(16, NA), lty = c(NA, 1), lwd = c(NA, 2))
finish_figure("Task 2.5.2: Normal Q-Q Plots of the Model Residuals")
```

```{r}
# Residual statistics (Gaussian residuals: skewness 0, excess kurtosis 0)
show_table("Task 2.5.3: Residual Statistics (Gaussian: mean 0, skewness 0, excess kurtosis 0)",
           data.frame(Model             = paste("Model", 1:5),
                      Mean              = dec(ifelse(abs(sapply(residual_list, mean)) < 5e-5, 0, sapply(residual_list, mean)), 4),
                      SD                = dec(sapply(residual_list, sd), 3),
                      Skewness          = dec(sapply(residual_list, skewness), 3),
                      "Excess Kurtosis" = dec(sapply(residual_list, excess_kurtosis), 3),
                      check.names = FALSE))
```

# ==================================================================================================
# Task 2.6: Select the 'Best' Regression Model (Comparison Table)
# ==================================================================================================

```{r}
# Model metrics from Tasks 2.2 - 2.4
model_comparison <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Model 1", "Model 2", "Model 3", "Model 4", "Model 5"),
  SSE = c(SSE_Model_1, SSE_Model_2, SSE_Model_3, SSE_Model_4, SSE_Model_5),
  Log_Likelihood = c(logLike_Model_1, logLike_Model_2, logLike_Model_3,
                     logLike_Model_4, logLike_Model_5),
  AIC = c(AIC_1, AIC_2, AIC_3, AIC_4, AIC_5),
  BIC = c(BIC_1, BIC_2, BIC_3, BIC_4, BIC_5)
)

# Model comparison
show_table("Task 2.6: Model Comparison (Delta = difference from the best model, 0 = best)",
           data.frame(Model               = model_comparison$Model,
                      AIC                 = dec(model_comparison$AIC),
                      BIC                 = dec(model_comparison$BIC),
                      # ADDITION: difference from the best model and residual shape
                      #           (AIC, BIC and residual criteria in one table)
                      "Delta AIC"         = dec(model_comparison$AIC - min(model_comparison$AIC)),
                      "Delta BIC"         = dec(model_comparison$BIC - min(model_comparison$BIC)),
                      "Residual Skewness" = dec(sapply(residual_list, skewness), 3),
                      "Residual Kurtosis" = dec(sapply(residual_list, excess_kurtosis), 3),
                      check.names = FALSE))

# Best model by each criterion
best_aic_model   <- model_comparison$Model[which.min(model_comparison$AIC)]
best_bic_model   <- model_comparison$Model[which.min(model_comparison$BIC)]
resid_departure  <- abs(sapply(residual_list, skewness)) + abs(sapply(residual_list, excess_kurtosis))
best_resid_model <- model_comparison$Model[which.min(resid_departure)]

# Selected model: lowest BIC (the brief asks for the 'true' model, which BIC targets)
model_list <- list("Model 1" = model_1, "Model 2" = model_2, "Model 3" = model_3,
                   "Model 4" = model_4, "Model 5" = model_5)
selected_model <- model_list[[best_bic_model]]

reason <- paste0(
  if (best_aic_model == best_bic_model) "Lowest AIC and lowest BIC"
  else "Lowest BIC (stronger penalty for extra parameters)",
  if (best_resid_model == best_bic_model) "; most Gaussian residuals"
  else paste0("; ", best_resid_model, " has slightly more Gaussian residuals (see Q-Q plots)"))

show_table("Task 2.6: Selected Best Model",
           data.frame("Lowest AIC" = best_aic_model, "Lowest BIC" = best_bic_model,
                      "Most Gaussian Residuals" = best_resid_model,
                      "Selected Model" = best_bic_model, Reason = reason,
                      check.names = FALSE))

```

# ==================================================================================================
# Task 2.7: Train/Test Split, Model Prediction and 95% Confidence Intervals
# ==================================================================================================

```{r}
# 70% training / 30% testing split
set.seed(42)

total_rows <- nrow(server_data)
train_size <- floor(0.70 * total_rows)
train_indices <- sample(seq_len(total_rows), size = train_size)

train_data <- server_data[train_indices, ]
test_data  <- server_data[-train_indices, ]

show_table("Training / Testing Split",
           data.frame(Dataset = c("Training", "Testing", "Total"),
                      Observations = c(nrow(train_data), nrow(test_data), total_rows),
                      Percentage = paste0(round(100 * c(nrow(train_data), nrow(test_data),
                                                        total_rows) / total_rows, 1), "%")))

# ==================================================================================================
# Task 2.7.1: Estimate model parameters using the training dataset
# ==================================================================================================


best_model_train <- lm(formula(selected_model), data = train_data)

# Parameter estimates from the training data
train_est <- coef(best_model_train)
show_table(paste("Task 2.7.1:", best_bic_model, "Parameters Estimated from the Training Data"),
           data.frame(Parameter = theta_name(names(train_est), names(train_est)),
                      Term      = term_name(names(train_est)),
                      Estimate  = num(unname(train_est))))

```
# ==================================================================================================
# Task 2.7.2: Compute the model's output/prediction on the testing data
# ==================================================================================================

```{r}
test_prediction <- predict(best_model_train, newdata = test_data)

test_results <- data.frame(
  Actual    = test_data$y,
  Predicted = test_prediction
)

first10 <- head(test_results, 10)
show_table("Task 2.7.2: Model Predictions on the Testing Data (first 10)",
           data.frame(Sample    = 1:nrow(first10),
                      Actual    = dec(first10$Actual),
                      Predicted = dec(first10$Predicted)))

# Prediction accuracy on the testing data (RMSE, MAE, R-squared)
test_errors <- test_results$Actual - test_results$Predicted
show_table("Task 2.7.2: Prediction Accuracy on the Testing Data",
           data.frame(Measure = c("RMSE (root mean squared error)", "MAE (mean absolute error)",
                                  "R-squared on testing data"),
                      Value   = c(dec(sqrt(mean(test_errors^2)), 3), dec(mean(abs(test_errors)), 3),
                                  dec(1 - sum(test_errors^2) /
                                        sum((test_results$Actual - mean(test_results$Actual))^2), 4))))
```

# ==================================================================================================
# Task 2.7.3: Compute the 95% confidence intervals and plot them with the prediction and test data
# ==================================================================================================

```{r}
confidence_95 <- predict(best_model_train, newdata = test_data,
                         interval = "confidence", level = 0.95)

test_results$Lower_95 <- confidence_95[, "lwr"]
test_results$Upper_95 <- confidence_95[, "upr"]

first10 <- head(test_results, 10)
show_table("Task 2.7.3: 95% Confidence Intervals of the Test Predictions (first 10)",
           data.frame(Sample    = 1:nrow(first10),
                      Actual    = dec(first10$Actual),
                      Predicted = dec(first10$Predicted),
                      "95% CI Lower" = dec(first10$Lower_95),
                      "95% CI Upper" = dec(first10$Upper_95),
                      check.names = FALSE))
```

```{r}
# Sort test samples by predicted value

sample_numbers <- seq_len(nrow(sorted_results))

# Plot test data, prediction and 95% confidence intervals

       legend = c("Testing data samples (actual y)", "Model prediction",

finish_figure(paste("Task 2.7.3:", best_bic_model,
                    "Test Predictions with 95% Confidence Intervals"))
```

# ==================================================================================================
# Task 3: Approximate Bayesian Computation (ABC) Using the Rejection ABC Method
# ==================================================================================================

```{r}
# ==================================================================================================
# Task 3.1: Select the 2 parameters with the largest absolute value (Task 2.1 estimates)
# ==================================================================================================

# Task 2.1 estimates of the selected model
model_weights <- coef(selected_model)

# All parameters, including the bias
telemetry_weights <- model_weights

if (length(telemetry_weights) < 2) {
  stop("The selected model must contain at least two predictor coefficients.")
}

sorted_weights <- sort(abs(telemetry_weights), decreasing = TRUE)

# Two largest absolute parameters
top_param_1_name <- names(sorted_weights)[1]
top_param_2_name <- names(sorted_weights)[2]

est_1 <- unname(model_weights[top_param_1_name])
est_2 <- unname(model_weights[top_param_2_name])

# Parameter labels for tables and plots
param_label_1 <- paste0(theta_name(top_param_1_name, names(model_weights)),
                        " (", term_name(top_param_1_name), ")")
param_label_2 <- paste0(theta_name(top_param_2_name, names(model_weights)),
                        " (", term_name(top_param_2_name), ")")

ranked_names <- names(sorted_weights)
show_table(paste("Task 3.1:", best_bic_model, "Task 2.1 Estimates, ranked by absolute value"),
           data.frame(Rank           = seq_along(ranked_names),
                      Parameter      = theta_name(ranked_names, names(model_weights)),
                      Term           = term_name(ranked_names),
                      Estimate       = num(unname(model_weights[ranked_names])),
                      "Absolute Value" = num(unname(sorted_weights)),
                      "Role in ABC"    = ifelse(seq_along(ranked_names) <= 2,
                                                "Estimated by ABC", "Fixed at Task 2.1 value"),
                      check.names = FALSE))

```

# ==================================================================================================
# Task 3.2: Define Uniform Prior Distributions
# ==================================================================================================

```{r}
set.seed(42)

num_samples <- 100000

# Prior range: estimate +/- 20% (standard error used if the estimate is near zero)
ols_se <- sqrt(diag(vcov(selected_model)))

prior_width_1 <- 0.20 * abs(est_1)
prior_width_2 <- 0.20 * abs(est_2)

if (prior_width_1 < 1e-10) {
  prior_width_1 <- 2 * ols_se[top_param_1_name]
}

if (prior_width_2 < 1e-10) {
  prior_width_2 <- 2 * ols_se[top_param_2_name]
}

prior_1_min <- est_1 - prior_width_1
prior_1_max <- est_1 + prior_width_1

prior_2_min <- est_2 - prior_width_2
prior_2_max <- est_2 + prior_width_2

if (!is.finite(prior_width_1) || !is.finite(prior_width_2) ||
    prior_width_1 <= 0 || prior_width_2 <= 0) {
  stop("Unable to define valid prior ranges. Check the estimates and standard errors.")
}

# Samples from the uniform priors
prior_1 <- runif(num_samples, min = prior_1_min, max = prior_1_max)
prior_2 <- runif(num_samples, min = prior_2_min, max = prior_2_max)

show_table("Task 3.2: Uniform Prior Ranges (estimate +/- 20%)",
           data.frame(Parameter   = c(param_label_1, param_label_2),
                      Estimate    = num(c(est_1, est_2)),
                      "Prior Lower" = num(c(prior_1_min, prior_2_min)),
                      "Prior Upper" = num(c(prior_1_max, prior_2_max)),
                      check.names = FALSE))

```

# ==================================================================================================
# Task 3.3: Perform Rejection ABC
# ==================================================================================================

```{r}
# Design matrix and observed output
X_matrix <- model.matrix(selected_model)
actual_y <- model.response(model.frame(selected_model))

# Other parameters fixed at their Task 2.1 estimates
frozen_weights <- model_weights

# Tolerance: 2% above the baseline SSE
baseline_SSE <- sum(residuals(selected_model)^2)
epsilon <- baseline_SSE * 1.02

show_table("Task 3.3: ABC Tolerance",
           data.frame(Quantity = c("Baseline SSE (Task 2.1 estimates)",
                                   "Tolerance epsilon (SSE x 1.02)"),
                      Value    = dec(c(baseline_SSE, epsilon))))

# SSE for each sampled parameter pair
error_values <- numeric(num_samples)

for (i in seq_len(num_samples)) {
  simulated_weights <- frozen_weights
  simulated_weights[top_param_1_name] <- prior_1[i]
  simulated_weights[top_param_2_name] <- prior_2[i]
  
  simulated_y <- as.vector(X_matrix %*% simulated_weights)
  error_values[i] <- sum((actual_y - simulated_y)^2)
}

# Accept samples within the tolerance
accepted_indices <- which(error_values <= epsilon)

accepted_1 <- prior_1[accepted_indices]
accepted_2 <- prior_2[accepted_indices]

acceptance_rate <- length(accepted_indices) / num_samples * 100

show_table("Task 3.3: Rejection ABC Sampling Result",
           data.frame("Prior Samples"    = formatC(num_samples, format = "d", big.mark = ","),
                      "Accepted Samples" = formatC(length(accepted_indices), format = "d", big.mark = ","),
                      "Acceptance Rate"  = paste0(round(acceptance_rate, 2), "%"),
                      check.names = FALSE))

if (length(accepted_indices) < 2) {
  stop("Too few samples were accepted. Consider increasing the ABC tolerance or prior sample count.")
}
```

# ==================================================================================================
# Task 3.4: Plot the Marginal and Joint Posterior Distributions
# ==================================================================================================

```{r}
# Marginal posterior with posterior mean and Task 2.1 estimate
start_figure(1, 2)

marginal_plot <- function(samples, estimate, label) {
  post_density <- density(samples)
  post_hist    <- hist(samples, breaks = 30, plot = FALSE)
  hist(samples, prob = TRUE, breaks = 30,
       ylim   = c(0, max(post_hist$density, post_density$y) * 1.15),
       col    = see_through(COLOR_MODEL, 0.6),
       border = "white",
       main   = paste("Marginal Posterior:", label),
       xlab   = label,
       ylab   = "Density")
  lines(post_density, col = COLOR_MODEL_DARK, lwd = 2)
  abline(v = mean(samples), col = COLOR_SUMMARY,   lwd = 2,   lty = 2)
  abline(v = estimate,      col = COLOR_REFERENCE, lwd = 2.5, lty = 3)
  legend("topright",
         legend = c("Posterior density", "Posterior mean", "Task 2.1 estimate"),
         col = c(COLOR_MODEL_DARK, COLOR_SUMMARY, COLOR_REFERENCE),
         lwd = c(2, 2, 2.5), lty = c(1, 2, 3), bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
}

marginal_plot(accepted_1, est_1, param_label_1)
marginal_plot(accepted_2, est_2, param_label_2)
finish_figure("Task 3.4.1: Marginal Posterior Distributions (Rejection ABC)")
```

```{r}
# Joint posterior
start_figure(1, 1)

plot(accepted_1, accepted_2,
     pch  = 16, cex = 0.6,
     col  = see_through(COLOR_MODEL, 0.3),
     xlab = param_label_1,
     ylab = param_label_2)

grid(col = "grey88", lty = 1)

# Density contours

    length(unique(accepted_1)) > 1 &&

}

# Posterior mean and Task 2.1 estimate
points(mean(accepted_1), mean(accepted_2), pch = 19, col = COLOR_SUMMARY,   cex = 1.6)
points(est_1, est_2,                       pch = 17, col = COLOR_REFERENCE, cex = 1.6)

legend("topright",
       legend = c("Accepted ABC samples", "Density contours",
                  "Posterior mean", "Task 2.1 estimate"),
       col = c(COLOR_MODEL, COLOR_MODEL_DARK, COLOR_SUMMARY, COLOR_REFERENCE),
       pch = c(16, NA, 19, 17), lty = c(NA, 1, NA, NA), lwd = c(NA, 1.5, NA, NA),
       bg = "white", box.col = "grey85", cex = 0.85)
finish_figure(paste("Task 3.4.2: Joint Posterior Distribution of", param_label_1, "and", param_label_2))
```

# ==================================================================================================
# Task 3.5: Summarise and Explain the ABC Results
# ==================================================================================================

```{r}
# Posterior summaries
posterior_mean_1 <- mean(accepted_1)
posterior_mean_2 <- mean(accepted_2)

posterior_sd_1 <- sd(accepted_1)
posterior_sd_2 <- sd(accepted_2)

posterior_interval_1 <- quantile(accepted_1, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
posterior_interval_2 <- quantile(accepted_2, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))

posterior_correlation <- cor(accepted_1, accepted_2)

show_table("Task 3.5: ABC Posterior Summary",
           data.frame(Parameter      = c(param_label_1, param_label_2),
                      "LS Estimate"    = num(c(est_1, est_2)),
                      "Posterior Mean" = num(c(posterior_mean_1, posterior_mean_2)),
                      "Posterior SD"   = num(c(posterior_sd_1, posterior_sd_2)),
                      "95% CI Lower"   = num(c(posterior_interval_1[1], posterior_interval_2[1])),
                      "95% CI Upper"   = num(c(posterior_interval_1[2], posterior_interval_2[2])),
                      check.names = FALSE))

# Prior range vs posterior interval (how much ABC reduced the uncertainty)
prior_widths     <- c(prior_1_max - prior_1_min, prior_2_max - prior_2_min)
posterior_widths <- c(diff(posterior_interval_1), diff(posterior_interval_2))
show_table("Task 3.5: Prior Range vs Posterior 95% Interval",
           data.frame(Parameter               = c(param_label_1, param_label_2),
                      "Prior Range Width"     = num(prior_widths),
                      "Posterior 95% Width"   = num(unname(posterior_widths)),
                      "Uncertainty Reduction" = paste0(dec(100 * (1 - posterior_widths / prior_widths), 1), "%"),
                      check.names = FALSE))

show_table("Task 3.5: Other ABC Results",
           data.frame(Quantity = c("Correlation between the 2 parameters", "Acceptance rate"),
                      Value    = c(dec(posterior_correlation, 4),
                                   paste0(round(acceptance_rate, 2), "%"))))
```
